stem: A term newborn has a head circumference measured at 12 hours of life and has scalp swelling after birth; how should this measurement be interpreted?

options.text: It is fully reliable from birth and should be interpreted without caution
It may be unreliable until day 3 to 4 because of moulding or scalp birth changes
It should not be measured until 6 weeks of age
It reflects only skull thickness and not intracranial contents
It is useful only if the anterior fontanelle is closed

explanation: Head circumference may be unreliable until day 3 to 4 of life because moulding and scalp birth changes can affect the measurement.
rationale: Early newborn head circumference can be misleading because moulding, cephalohaematoma, and caput succedaneum can alter the result; interpretation improves after the first few days of life.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because newborn measurements may be unreliable in the first few days.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because moulding and scalp birth changes can make the head circumference measurement unreliable until day 3 to 4 of life.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because the measurement should still be taken in the newborn period; it does not need to be delayed until 6 weeks.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because head circumference is used as a proxy for skull and intracranial growth, not just skull thickness.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because the reliability of head circumference does not depend on the anterior fontanelle being closed.
